title: Links
summary: Connect pages with the a element and choose between absolute, relative and in-page links.

quiz.q: Which attribute holds the destination of a link?
quiz.explain: `href` (hypertext reference) holds the address. `src` is used by images, not links.

quiz.q: Complete the link so it opens in a new tab.
quiz.explain: `target="_blank"` asks the browser to use a new tab or window.

quiz.q: Which of these is a **relative** URL?
quiz.explain: A relative URL has no website name. It is found by following the path from the current file.

quiz.q: Click the line that will not jump to the section.
quiz.explain: The target needs `id="contact"`. The old `name` attribute on a heading is ignored.

exercise.task:
Add navigation links to `index.html`. - An absolute link to `https://developer.mozilla.org` with the text `MDN`, opening in a new tab (`target="_blank"`) with `rel="noopener"`. - A relative link to `about.html` with the text `About me`. - A link to `#contact` with the text `Contact`. - A heading `

Contact

` for the link to jump to.
hints: A link is text. Make three of them, then add the heading with an id.
Absolute addresses start with https://. Relative ones are just a file name. In-page links start with # and match an id exactly.

MDN About me Contact

Contact

checks.name: A link goes to https://developer.mozilla.org with the text MDN
checks.hint: Use href="https://developer.mozilla.org" and the link text MDN.

checks.name: The MDN link opens in a new tab
checks.hint: Add target="_blank" to the MDN link.

checks.name: A relative link to about.html says "About me"
